title: Gillett-Watson-Goodale counterpart archive register
scope: Digitized counterpart sources for testing whether the Southwick nursery supply system documented from the Blaschka workshop side can be independently connected to Harvard procurement or taxonomy through Sereno Watson.

hypothesis.statement: Sereno Watson may have occupied a taxonomic or procurement junction between George Lincoln Goodale and Edward Gillett during the same period in which living American botanical references were supplied to the Blaschka workshop.
hypothesis.guard: Date adjacency, shared recipient and invoice survival do not establish a Blaschka transaction. Promotion requires content-level evidence from the letters or invoices.

source_environment.source_status: BHL metadata directly indexes the individual correspondence parts; several parts are mirrored as PDFs by Zenodo/Plazi.

gillett_sequence.sender_context: Edward Gillett / Southwick nursery correspondence cluster

goodale_sequence.date_guard: BHL metadata renders year in brackets

workshop_comparison_anchor.event: California bulb supplied by Gillett & Horsford in the previous year had flowered at Hosterwitz; colour differed from published descriptions; workshop intended modelling while expecting Goodale-side determination.
workshop_comparison_anchor.relationship_to_counterpart_cluster: The first indexed 1891 Gillett-to-Watson letter is dated five days later, on 24 July 1891.
workshop_comparison_anchor.guard: Temporal adjacency is a retrieval cue only and is not evidence of correspondence about this Fritillaria.

catalogue_context.title: Southwick Nurseries 1890 wholesale catalogue of North American perennials, new Tigridias, California bulbs, etc
catalogue_context.holding_institution: U.S. Department of Agriculture, National Agricultural Library
catalogue_context.research_value: Directly shows California bulbs as a Southwick commercial stock category in the year the workshop later said its California Fritillaria bulb was sent.

catalogue_context.title: Gillett & Horsford's 1890 descriptive catalogue of wild flowers, shrubs, trees and vines
catalogue_context.holding_institution: U.S. Department of Agriculture, National Agricultural Library

failure_conditions: Gillett-Watson correspondence concerns unrelated herbarium/taxonomic exchange only.
Invoices are Watson's private purchases or belong to another transaction.
Goodale-Watson letters are unrelated to plant procurement or identification for the Blaschka programme.
No Blaschka, Hosterwitz or relevant supply terms occur in the cluster.
research_value_if_negative: Even a negative linkage would provide a same-year control showing the ordinary structure of Harvard-nursery exchange against which the Blaschka supply chain can be compared.
